subject: Persistent frame starvation & WebSocket timeouts impacting Stratos AI - exec attention
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@stratos.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ariell@stratos.ai, procurement@stratos.ai
Date: 2028-07-28 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Realtime feed - intermittent silent frames and socket drops (urgent)

Kimberly —

We're seeing a surge in dropped frames and long gaps in our realtime response stream starting ~08:50 UTC this morning. Several of our agents hit repeated WebSocket timeouts (client sees 504 / silent frame >10s) and the service returns 5xx at higher rates during the burst. Latency is spiking (p50 ~420ms -> p95 ~2.9s for streaming tokens) and throughput appears to fall off when keepalives are triggered. This is impacting customer-facing pipelines (inference for live chat) across multiple regions in us-west.

Attached is a small network trace and our error sample. We need an immediate mitigation and a timeline for root cause. Please escalate if necessary.

Sanjay
CTO, Stratos AI
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@stratos.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-28 09:25:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Realtime feed - intermittent silent frames and socket drops (urgent)

Sanjay — thanks for the quick heads up. I'm escalating immediately.

Immediate actions we are taking:
- Routing your traffic to an isolated capacity pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects (temporary).
- Increasing proxy keepalive timeout and disabling chunked buffering at the edge for your tenant for the next hour to see if it reduces frame coalescing.
- Karthik is pulling live traces from our proxy and runtime; Marissa is standing by for exec-level updates.

We will reply in 30 minutes with status and a short mitigation plan. Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously.

—Kimberly
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-28 09:42:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Realtime feed - intermittent silent frames and socket drops (urgent)

Quick technical summary from the runtime team:

Observations:
- Between 08:48-09:20 UTC we saw a pattern where token emission stalls for 6-12s before either resuming or the client-triggered heartbeat closes the socket.
- Proxy (edge) logs show chunked transfer flush coalescing combined with backpressure signals from runtime -> spikes in per-connection queue depth.
- Error rate correlates with a small subset of model variants on our m60 pools where a kernel path regresses under mixed quantized sequences.
- No apparent network packet loss on our backbone; customer pcap shows client retransmits consistent with delayed TCP ACKs.

Immediate mitigations applied (done at 09:34 UTC):
- Drained affected connections to a warm fallback model (slightly smaller context) to avoid the problematic kernel path.
- Disabled Nginx proxy chunked buffering for the tenant and raised the upstream read timeout to 35s; reduced per-connection batching on the runtime side.
- Enabled verbose token-level tracing for impacted sessions and uploaded sample traces to shared drive.

Next steps (owner):
- Karthik: complete live trace correlation and identify kernel/quant path (2-4h).
- Kimberly: coordinate customer comms and temporary SLA ask (15m).
- Marissa: prepare an exec note if the issue persists or if SEV is declared (30m).

Karthik
Applied ML / Runtime
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-28 10:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Realtime feed - intermittent silent frames and socket drops (urgent)

Looping in leadership context — this is beginning to look like a production reliability incident affecting an expanding customer. If Karhthik's kernel path hypothesis holds, we may need a temporary capacity switch for affected customers and a credit/SLA remediation ask.

Suggested immediate exec asks:
- Approve a 24-hour elevated support window and 10% credit for impacted production queries if we can't restore stable streaming within 3 hours. (Draft SLA attached)
- Greenlight limited traffic relocation to a dedicated m100 pool for Stratos while we root cause (cost impact estimate attached).

Kimberly — please get a customer-facing status that sets expectations and asks for permission to relocate traffic. I will prepare the exec note for leadership and legal.

-Marissa
VP, Customer Reliability
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@stratos.ai>
Cc: Arielle Park <arielle@stratos.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-28 10:28:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Realtime feed - intermittent silent frames and socket drops (urgent)

Sanjay / Arielle —

Update and ask: thank you for the packet capture and error samples. We've applied temporary mitigations (routing to fallback model variant, disabling chunked buffering on your tenant, raising proxy timeouts) and are observing a reduction in 5xx spikes and longer frames. However, we want to offer a temporary dedicated pool relocation to avoid recurrence while we finish the kernel analysis.

Can we get approval to move Stratos traffic to an isolated m100 pool for the next 24 hours? This will have a cost delta; we've attached the proposed temporary SLA and the estimated cost difference. If approved, we can cutover in ~20 minutes. If you prefer, we can instead maintain the current mitigations and continue investigation without relocation.

Appreciate quick confirmation so we can act.

—Kimberly
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@stratos.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ariell@stratos.ai, procurement@stratos.ai
Date: 2028-07-28 11:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Realtime feed - intermittent silent frames and socket drops (urgent)

Kimberly —

Approve the dedicated pool relocation for 24 hours. We'll accept the cost delta for now, please go ahead. Also please keep us updated on root cause and any SLA credits. Procurement copied for billing.

Sanjay

On Tue, Jul 28, 2028 at 10:45 AM kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
> Understood — cutover scheduled to begin at 11:10 UTC. I'll confirm when traffic is fully on the isolated pool.


[Internal follow-up summary — 2028-07-28 17:05 UTC]
Final internal note (to leadership and infra): by 15:00 UTC the dedicated pool cutover completed and incident rates returned to baseline for Stratos. Karthik's trace correlation identified a kernel path regression when mixed int8/float16 quantized sequences hit a specific attention optimizer on m60 kernels; remediation options being evaluated: kernel patch, forced quantization profile change for the affected model variants, or permanently relocating affected customers to m100 until a patch is validated.

Action items:
- Karthik: produce a detailed RCA and timeline for kernel fix (ETA 72h).
- Marissa: finalize the SLA remediation offer and credit terms (24h).
- Tessa: update exec incident timeline and notify Sales leadership.
- Kimberly: follow up with Stratos on final postmortem and next steps.

Attachments referenced: network_trace_0728.pcap; service_error_snippets.txt; proposed_sla_temporary_ask.docx
